name: aicontribcheck
one_liner: Offline AI-contribution-policy detector for open-source repositories: scans CONTRIBUTING / README / AGENTS.md / .github/ policy files for machine-readable statements about whether AI-authored contributions are allowed, banned, or conditional, plus any disclosure/attribution obligations, and emits a structured verdict.
problem: arXiv 2607.26819 ('A First Look at Coding Agents' Compliance with AI Contribution Rules in Open-Source Communities', 2026-07-29) finds that coding agents never proactively retrieve contribution rules and cannot refuse contributions in AI-banned repositories without explicit prompts. The missing primitive is a small offline tool that, given a repository checkout, scans a canonical set of policy files and emits a structured verdict (allowed | banned | conditional | unknown | conflict) plus any required disclosures, attribution obligations, and human-review requirements. aicontribcheck is that primitive. Ten documented rules (AICONTRIB-001 through AICONTRIB-010) cover explicit ban, explicit allow, disclosure-required, attribution obligation (DCO / CLA / copyright assignment / signed-off-by), human-review-required, tests-required, named-AI-tool mention (evidence-only), non-commercial licence detected on the LICENSE file, unknown-policy rollup, and cross-file conflict.
